vopros: How do I get AI assistants to recommend my company to customers in the US?

vyzhimka.tekst:
You can’t make an AI assistant recommend your company on demand. You can make it easier for assistants that search the web to discover, understand, and trust your business—and then track whether that’s working.

### Start with the basics

1. **Make your site accessible to search systems.** Ensure important pages are public, indexable, and readable as text—not only embedded in images or loaded in ways crawlers can’t access. For ChatGPT search, OpenAI says publishers should allow **OAI-SearchBot** in `robots.txt` if they want their content to be discoverable and cited. For Google’s AI features, pages must be indexed and eligible to appear in regular Google Search.
2. **Explain clearly what you sell and who it’s for.** Create useful pages for your products, services, industries, locations, pricing, and common customer questions. State relevant facts directly, keep details current, and support claims with evidence.
3. **Build credibility beyond your own website.** Earn accurate coverage, reviews, expert references, and mentions on reputable industry sites and directories. Keep your business name, address, phone number, product details, and service area consistent across listings.
4. **Use ordinary SEO and sound site structure.** Make pages easy to navigate and link to; use descriptive titles and headings; and add structured data where it accurately reflects visible information. Google says there’s no special schema or AI-specific file required for its AI search features.
5. **Make recommendations easy to justify.** Publish concrete differentiators, comparison information, customer outcomes, certifications, and transparent limitations. Avoid unsupported superlatives, fake reviews, or mass-produced pages—they can erode trust.

### Measure and improve

Test realistic prompts your US customers might ask, such as “best [type of provider] for [need] in [city].” Check several assistants periodically, note whether your company appears and which sources they cite, and compare that with referral traffic and leads. Improve pages and third-party information where the answers are unclear or inaccurate. Visibility varies by query, location, assistant, and time; there’s no guaranteed placement.

results.snippet:
Google Search Central's core guidance on AI Overviews is that there is no special AI-Overviews markup or separate AI index.
The same helpful, people-first, high-quality content and standard structured data that ranks in organic Search is what surfaces in AI Overviews, drawn from the same index and judged by the same E-E-A-T signals.
...
Content that performs well in organic search has a higher baseline probability of being cited in AI Overviews.
...
On content quality, Google Search Central's guidance aligns with their long-standing E-E-A-T framework: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness.
Content demonstrating first-hand experience, subject matter expertise, and authoritative sourcing is preferred by the AI Overview system.
...
Google Search Central has long recommended structured data for helping Google understand content.
Schema markup -- Article, FAQ, HowTo, Organization, Author -- provides machine-readable context that any AI system, including AI Overviews, can use to evaluate and categorize your content.
...
No schema type guarantees AI Overview citation.
Structured data helps Google understand your content, which can improve citation likelihood, but it is not a citation trigger.
...
Google recommends helpful, people-first content that demonstrates E-E-A-T: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness.

In late May 2026, Google published its first official guidance on how AI Overviews and AI Mode work.
It is the clearest thing the company has said on the subject, and it points directly at the fundamentals: fast, accessible websites, content that reflects genuine expertise, and strong local reputation signals.
...
The guidance lives in Google Search Central’s documentation under “Optimizing for generative AI features on Google Search.”
It was announced at Google I/O 2026 and covers AI Overviews, AI Mode, and the emerging category of agentic search experiences.
...
Its generative AI features pull from the same Search index as traditional results.
...
Three themes run through the document: foundational SEO, demonstrable expertise, and trust and local relevance.
...
The guidance explicitly references crawlability, site structure, mobile usability, page speed, and internal linking, and these same factors affect both traditional search visibility and how AI Overviews retrieve content.
...
**Google explicitly prioritizes what it calls “non-commodity content,” meaning content that goes beyond what anyone with a search engine could produce.**
...
The guidance calls out Google Business Profile, reviews, citation consistency, and local mentions as signals that carry weight in both traditional and AI-powered local results.
...
Structured data continues to matter for rich results, including review stars, FAQ boxes, and local business details.
But Google is explicit that there is no special schema.org markup for AI search.
There is no AI-specific type or new property you need to add.
...
The short version: existing, accurate, validated structured data is what matters.
